newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SOUNESS ANGRY WITH BENALI -- AND THE REFEREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUNESS ANGRY WITH BENALI -- AND THE REFEREE.

text.p: Southampton manager Graeme Souness launched a blistering verbal assault on referee Graham Poll after his struggling Southampton side were sent stumbling out of the F.A. Cup at Reading.
The premier league's bottom team had Francis Benali and Robbie Slater shown the red card as they crashed to a 3-1 defeat.
Benali was dismissed for elbowing Trevor Morley and then midfielder Robbie Slater was sent off in the final minute for swearing at a linesman.

By then it was all over, goals from James Lambert and Darren Caskey -- both courtesy of shocking defensive errors -- sandwiching Egil Ostenstad's goal for Saints before Morley converted from the spot after picking himself up after being elbowed by Benali.
But Souness was adamant that the game should not have been played and appeared to confront the referee at the final whistle although he denied having said anything.
What he did say to reporters afterwards was strong enough and could lead to him facing trouble from the English Football Association.
"I met the referee this morning and told him then that it wasn't fit to play," said Souness standing just a matter of yards from the rock hard playing surface.
"He came out with two incredible statements. The first that it was like playing on the pitch in August.
"The second was that it would be okay if the players went at it only 90 per cent.
"I told him it was a Cup tie, how could he expect players to go 90 per cent. That's incredible."
Souness then added: "Mr Poll has a reputation among the professionals in the game as somebody who is trying to make a name for himself.
"It's the second time in a week that he's made teams play when the pitch wasn't playable.
"As I said he's a referee who is trying to make a name for himself and he's done that today."
The referee declined to answer questions directly although he did confirm through a Reading steward that Benali was sent off for elbowing Morley and that Slater's dismissal came for swearing.
He added that in his view the pitch had been playable both on Friday and on Saturday when he inspected the pitch with the two managers before the game.
Regarding the dismissals, Souness said he had sympathy with Australian Slater although not with club skipper Benali, sent off for the third time this season.
"Slater maintains that he didn't swear at the linesman," said Souness.
"For the other one though if the elbow made contact then he deserved to be sent off. I haven't seen Francis Benali but if he made contact he deserved to go."
Souness accepted that Reading had deserved to win and Jimmy Quinn, Reading's joint player-boss, admitted he could not have been more pleased with the way his side had performed.
"We kept our discipline and caused them a lot of problems with the way we played," said Quinn. "I couldn't ask for more.
"We had a lot of chances. The only disappointment was that we let them back in it at 1-1 but then we kicked on and could have scored more by the end."
Southampton are still in the league cup, but are out of the F.A. Cup and bottom of the premier league. The next few months look like being very tough indeed for the men from The Dell.
